newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rights group says PLO police tortured man to death.
newsitem.headline: Rights group says PLO police tortured man to death.

text.p: Palestinian security forces tortured to death a Palestinian during interrogation in the West Bank self-rule enclave of Nablus, a Palestinian human rights group said on Saturday.
Palestinian officials confirmed the man, Yussef Ismail al-Baba, had died, but they did not say how. They said they were investigating the cause of his death.

"This morning ...Yussef Ismail al-Baba, 32, died from wounds inflicted from torture during interrogation by the Palestinian military intelligence," a statement issued to the media by the Jerusalem-based Palestinian Society for the Protection of Human Rights and the Environment said.
It said the incident occurred in a Nablus lockup.

Nablus police commander Jamil Hamdi told Reuters: "It is true that Yussef al-Baba has died. We have sent the prosecutor general to investigate and we are waiting for a medical report on the cause of his death."
Baba was arrested on January 3 on suspicion of making an improper property sale, the human rights organisation said.
Human rights groups have accused Palestinian security forces of systematic torture of prisoners and have charged that the Palestinian Authority is not doing enough to end the abuse.
The Palestinian Authority denies systematic torture but it has investigated cases of prisoners' deaths in detention and has vowed to fight abuses.
In August, a Palestinian military court sentenced three Palestinian policemen to long jail terms after it found them guilty of torturing a prisoner to death.

According to the human rights organisation, nine Palestinians have been tortured to death while under interrogation since the Palestinian Authority began taking control of the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank in 1994 under interim peace deals with Israel.
